{"id":"49cfb010-8de0-48d4-85bd-e7dd33b5de39","state":"COMPLETED","response":"# Independent referee report: Erdős Problem #99

28 October 2026 · Scope: global minimum-diameter packings, original physical labels, arbitrary grain orientations

Verdict: Erdős Problem #99 remains unsolved. I obtain a rigorous, explicitly quantified same-nnn, strictly smaller-diameter competitor theorem for two near-triangular grains separated by a sufficiently depleted seam. It permits arbitrary relative orientations, counts every original point, and yields a conditional exclusion theorem for global minimizers.

The unrestricted target is not proved. In particular, an O(D)O(D)O(D) bound on seam corrections without control of its leading coefficient does not suffice for the comparison. I also give an explicit construction showing why a nonzero orientation mismatch alone cannot supply a uniform seam penalty.

The distinction is substantive: the result excludes a defined class of possible global minimizers, not all triangle-free two-grain minimizers.

## 1. The exact problem and the global comparison

For n≥2n\ge2n≥2, define

Dn=min⁡A⊂R2∣A∣=n∣p−q∣≥1,p≠qdiam⁡(A).D_n=\min_{\substack{A\subset\mathbb R^2\\ |A|=n\\ |p-q|\ge1,\ p\ne q}} \operatorname{diam}(A).Dn​=A⊂R2∣A∣=n∣p−q∣≥1,p=q​min​diam(A).

The minimum is attained by compactness after fixing one point at the origin and restricting to a bounded sublevel set.

Erdős asks whether, for sufficiently large nnn, every configuration attaining DnD_nDn​ contains three points with all pairwise distances exactly one. His 1994 statement is explicit in §3.2, p. 268. Erdős Problems

Primary source: [P. Erdős, Some Problems in Number Theory, Combinatorics and Combinatorial Geometry, Mathematica Pannonica 5 (1994), 261–269](https://mathematica-pannonica.ttk.pte.hu/articles/mp05-2/mp05-2-261-269.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com).

a=32,a=\frac{\sqrt3}{2},a=23​​,

n≤∣K∣a+P(K)2+1.(2)n\le \frac{|K|}{a}+\frac{P(K)}2+1. \tag{2}n≤a∣K∣​+2P(K)​+1.(2)

## 2. New scoped result: exact two-grain replacement criterion

### Theorem — full-original-label seam replacement

Let AAA be any finite unit-separated planar configuration of diameter DDD, and write

n=∣A∣,K=conv⁡(A).n=|A|,\qquad K=\operatorname{conv}(A).n=∣A∣,K=conv(A).

Step 1: Injectively associate original points with lattice sites.

Thus each assigned original determines a distinct lattice site. No original labels are discarded.

The Voronoi cell of a unit triangular-lattice site is a regular hexagon of area aaa and circumradius

Hence a translated lattice disk of diameter D−δD-\deltaD−δ contains more than nnn unit-separated points. Select exactly nnn of them.

If their minimum separation is greater than one, rescale downward to make it exactly one; their diameter cannot increase.

The result is an admissible nnn-point packing of diameter strictly less than DDD.

This proves the theorem. □\square□

## 4. Consequence for actual global minimizers

The preceding theorem can be linked to global optimality without assuming the project's unreviewed population-reserve coefficient.

First, every global minimizer with diameter DDD has an almost circular convex hull in the precise asymptotic area sense.

Indeed, for each r<D/2r<D/2r<D/2, the translation-averaging construction (8) cannot produce nnn sites inside BrB_rBr​, since that would contradict global optimality. Therefore

πr2a≤n−1.\frac{\pi r^2}{a}\le n-1.aπr2​≤n−1.

Letting r↑D/2r\uparrow D/2r↑D/2,

n−1≥πD24a.(11)n-1\ge\frac{\pi D^2}{4a}. \tag{11}n−1≥4aπD2​.(11)

Apply Oler's inequality (2), followed by P(K)≤πDP(K)\le\pi DP(K)≤πD:

πD24−aπD2≤∣K∣≤πD24.(12)\boxed{ \frac{\pi D^2}{4}-\frac{a\pi D}{2} \le |K|\le\frac{\pi D^2}{4}. } \tag{12}4πD2​−2aπD​≤∣K∣≤4πD2​.​(12)

Thus the area deficit from the optimal disk is O(D)O(D)O(D), not O(D2)O(D^2)O(D2).

For any sequence of globally minimizing configurations with D→∞D\to\inftyD→∞, translate the midpoint of a diametral pair to the origin and divide coordinates by DDD. The resulting convex hulls have diameter one, contain the two diametral endpoints, and have areas approaching π/4\pi/4π/4.

By compactness of bounded planar convex bodies, every subsequence has a Hausdorff-convergent subsubsequence. The isodiametric equality case forces every limit to be the radius-1/21/21/2 disk centered at the diametral midpoint. Therefore the entire sequence converges to that disk.

In particular, for any line through this midpoint,

∣K∩{∣x∣<2}∣=4D+o(D).(13)\left|K\cap\{|x|<2\}\right| =4D+o(D). \tag{13}∣K∩{∣x∣<2}∣=4D+o(D).(13)

The centered width-four strip therefore eventually satisfies S≥3.9DS\ge3.9DS≥3.9D.

Global-minimizer exclusion theorem. For all sufficiently large DDD, no global diameter-DDD minimizer can have a line through the midpoint of a diametral pair such that all but at most D/4D/4D/4 of its original points lie outside the width-four strip and, on each side, are within 1/201/201/20 of some unit triangular lattice. The two lattices may have unrelated orientations and translations.

The proof is (12)–(13), followed by the effective corollary.

This is an exact consequence about global optimizers. It does not assume that a globally optimal configuration itself comes from a lattice.

## 5. Why this does not settle the arbitrary two-grain target

The missing implication is now numerical and structural, rather than hidden in a packing heuristic.

For an arbitrary two-grain candidate, one must establish a full-original-label decomposition whose actual seam area SSS, lattice-coordinate error η\etaη, and exceptional count mmm satisfy (3).

Knowing merely that

m=O(D)m=O(D)m=O(D)

does not imply (3). The constant in the O(D)O(D)O(D) term can consume the entire favorable seam-area contribution.

There is a second, more fundamental obstruction to extracting such a constant from disorientation alone.

Take the unit triangular-lattice crop

AR0=Λ∩BR.A_R^0=\Lambda\cap B_R.AR0​=Λ∩BR​.

Split the original sites into left and right halves. Apply a small vertical stretch 1+β1+\beta1+β to both halves and an additional rotation through angle α>0\alpha>0α>0 to the right half.

Choose

0<α,β<2R−4.0<\alpha,\beta<2R^{-4}.0<α,β<2R−4.

Each moved point is displaced by O(R−3)O(R^{-3})O(R−3). The minimum pairwise distance remains at least 1−O(R−3)1-O(R^{-3})1−O(R−3). Rescale the whole finite configuration by the reciprocal of its actual minimum distance.

The resulting packing has exactly the original number of labels, minimum separation one, and diameter differing from that of AR0A_R^0AR0​ by at most

O(R−2).O(R^{-2}).O(R−2).

For generic choices of α,β\alpha,\betaα,β, it is also triangle-free. To justify this last assertion, for each fixed triple the condition that its three squared distances agree defines analytic equalities in α,β\alpha,\betaα,β. These equalities cannot hold identically: at α=0\alpha=0α=0, varying the vertical stretch cannot leave three distinct planar points equilateral for every stretch. The exceptional parameter sets therefore have empty interior; there are only finitely many triples.

Thus two distinct, extremely near-triangular grain orientations can coexist with no fixed positive diameter penalty relative to the original lattice crop. This is a constructive obstruction to inferring a uniform seam-energy or population penalty merely from nonzero misorientation.

It is not an example of a globally optimal packing, nor a counterexample to the existence of a strict competitor. For fixed, substantially different orientations, a positive grain-boundary cost may still be provable. What fails is the proposed uniform inference without a quantitative mismatch or defect hypothesis.

The distinction matters: a bound of O(R−2)O(R^{-2})O(R−2) against a lattice reference does not determine the difference from DnD_nDn​.

## 6. Audit of the other stated project routes

The earlier conditional local-hexagon result attributed to w66_620 is consistent with the sharp Voronoi-cell equality theorem. In unit-separated normalization, the minimal bounded Voronoi-cell area is a=3/2a=\sqrt3/2a=3​/2, with equality at a regular hexagon. Mazel–Stuhl–Suhov's 2022 proof supplies a modern rigorous source for that classical equality case. arxiv.org

However, local ε\varepsilonε-hexagonal geometry does not by itself produce two globally coherent lattice coordinate maps with errors bounded by 1/201/201/20. Local orientation and phase errors can accumulate. Nor does the estimate Oε(D)O_\varepsilon(D)Oε​(D) supply the small exceptional-point coefficient required above.

Similarly, the w66_634 alternative representative controls contact isolates, not all unmatched physical labels. The saturated-chamber result attributed to w66_625 does not establish global diameter optimality. The w66_614 nonglobal KKT construction correctly warns that local stress and boundary rigidity are insufficient substitutes for a same-nnn competitor.

The pinned October 15 reserve,

The infimum need not be attained. Near-triangular rhombic lattices, with basis angle θ>π/3\theta>\pi/3θ>π/3, independently show that triangle-free unit-contact patterns can have density approaching 2/32/\sqrt32/3​. Neither observation decides exact global attainment.

## 7. Historical priority and final disposition

The relevant chronology is established by the following primary works, not by this project's later computational or structural investigations.

Historical primary sources

Establishes eventual nonlattice optimality in the relevant finite-packing setting. Excluding lattice configurations is not the same as excluding unit equilateral triangles.
- Mazel–Stuhl–Suhov (2022): [Minimal Area of a Voronoi Cell in a Packing of Unit Circles](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.03255?utm_source=chatgpt.com). Gives a modern proof of the classical sharp local hexagonal-area inequality.

The seam-replacement inequality (3) and its stated numerical corollary are derived here from these classical tools. I do not claim established publication priority or that a similar conditional deduction is absent elsewhere.

Final assessment: The requested universal arbitrary-mismatch competitor is not established. What is proved is a quantitative full-original-label replacement theorem and an eventual exclusion of global minimizers with a specified, sufficiently underfilled two-grain seam. What remains is a theorem converting generic two-grain near-triangular structure—including all seam corrections—into a strict inequality like (3), or a different exact same-nnn global comparison that works without a positive seam-density budget.

No KKT sufficiency, exact triangle conclusion, globally optimal counterexample, or unrestricted solution is claimed."}

Complete rigorous negative result for the disk-maximality route

1. Global optimality is indispensable. The lattice-population lower bound (1) is obtained by contradicting a smaller-diameter nnn-point competitor. It does not follow merely from unit separation, a saturated packing, KKT stationarity, or fixed-hull maximality.

2. The perimeter and area inequalities must match the hull class. The parallelogram bounds are simultaneously sharp for squares but the perimeter bound fails for general quadrilaterals. Equations (16) and (17) repair that extension.

3. A diameter cutoff is a necessary condition, not an optimizer classification. If D≤CkRD\le C_k^{\mathrm R}D≤CkR​, nothing here implies that a kkk-sided hull is globally optimal, or even that it supports a packing of the relevant cardinality.

A large hull-vertex count, near-disk area, small Oler slack, or near-hexagonal local geometry does not produce an exact unit equilateral triple. The anisotropic stretching obstruction rules out a uniform triangle-free near-optimality gap.

## 7. Referee verdict

The small-nnn investigation establishes three distinct conclusions.

First, the certified n=8n=8n=8 constructions show that exact global optimality does not uniformly determine whether an optimizer contains a unit equilateral triangle. An identical globally optimal hull supports both outcomes, and the triangle-generating interior contacts can have universally zero stress multipliers.

Second, a fully supported positive stress and maximal first-order active rank can coexist with a triangle-free configuration, as in the numerical n=9n=9n=9 candidate. Consequently stress positivity and first-order rigidity alone are insufficient as global certificates.

Third, strict inactivity can persist at the endpoint itself, not merely among near-optimal configurations; the n=8n=8n=8 example proves this globally, while the numerical n=11n=11n=11 candidate illustrates it at another cardinality.

None of these findings proves or disproves the sufficiently-large-nnn Erdős conjecture. The outstanding gap remains an all-label, arbitrary-competitor global argument capable of distinguishing true diameter minimizers from stressed or saturated nonglobal configurations.

The exact small-case conclusions rest on the 1951 and 1999 published global theorems; the independent computations verify shapes, contacts, numerical stresses, affine behavior, and rigorous feasible upper bounds, but do not replace those global theorems.
